messages:
alice_sdk: Ran into a reproducible bug with the async Python SDK + asyncio timeouts that can cause request replay and duplicate side-effects. Put a tiny sample app below.

alice_sdk: sample repro:
```py
# sample_app.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key="x") as client:
        try:
            # force a short outer timeout to provoke a transport hang/use-case
            await client.create_completion(model="x", prompt="do thing")
        except Exception as e:
            print('caught', e)

asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(main(), timeout=3))
```

alice_sdk: Observed: asyncio.wait_for raises TimeoutError to caller, but SDK logged a retry and server processed the request, so side-effect occurred twice (duplicate DB row).

ben_infra: can you share client logs and request id? Is this only when using asyncio.wait_for or also if you pass a client-level timeout?

alice_sdk: logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-14T10:01:12.345Z DEBUG sending request id=req-abc POST /v1/completions
2026-02-14T10:01:14.999Z WARN transport timeout during send id=req-abc
2026-02-14T10:01:15.001Z ERROR context manager __aexit__ closing client with inflight send id=req-abc
2026-02-14T10:01:15.100Z INFO retrying request id=req-abc -> new-id=req-abc-retry1
2026-02-14T10:01:15.200Z INFO request succeeded id=req-abc-retry1
```

alice_sdk: So the outer task timed out, but the transport retried immediately after seeing a timeout and succeeded.

charlie_oncall: We saw a related incident last month. When a socket write hangs and the parent task is cancelled, __aexit__ doesn't always cancel the low-level send; SDK treats transport timeouts as transient and replays.

charlie_oncall: Short-term workaround: attach an idempotency key for mutating endpoints, or await client.aclose() before letting outer timeout drop the task.

ben_infra: Sounds like two fixes needed: (1) ensure __aexit__ waits for inflight send tasks to be deterministically cancelled/observed, (2) change retry semantics: do not auto-retry when the transport reports an ambiguous/uncertain send (i.e. caller cancellation).

ben_infra: Proposed approach: when a transport write times out or is cancelled, raise a special UncertainSendError instead of triggering immediate retry. Retry policy: only auto-retry on clear transient network errors, or when idempotency_key is present. Example pseudo-change:
```py
# transport.py
async def _send_with_guard(request):
    try:
        await transport.send(request)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        # caller cancelled -> treat as definite cancellation, do NOT auto-retry
        raise
    except TransportTimeoutError as e:
        # mark uncertain so caller decides to retry or attach idempotency
        raise UncertainSendError(original=e)

# retry policy: if UncertainSendError -> skip auto-retry unless idempotency_key present
```

charlie_oncall: +1. Add unit tests with a fake server that delays ack after receiving bytes to verify we don't double-apply without an idempotency key. Also an integration test for asyncio.wait_for scenarios.

alice_sdk: I filed an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4523 with the sample app and logs. I'll draft a PR to: (a) make __aexit__ wait for send tasks to finish or be cancelled, (b) surface UncertainSendError on transport timeouts, (c) update retry policy to avoid auto-replay without idempotency.

devex-bot: Issue #4523 created by alice_sdk: "async context + outer timeout can cause POST replay; duplicate side effects". Labels: bug, sdk-python, high-priority.

ben_infra: Also add a migration note in docs recommending idempotency keys for mutating endpoints and caution about using asyncio.wait_for with short timeouts. We might also lengthen backoff or require an explicit verify/ack endpoint before retrying in cancellation cases.

alice_sdk: I'll post the PR link once ready and include tests. cc @charlie_oncall for incident trace to reproduce timing.

charlie_oncall: Happy to attach trace and test harness. :thumbsup:
